messages:
raj: Heads-up — ran a batch of paged-attention (+FlashVariant) microbenchmarks across SM80 (CUDA 12) and SM90 (CUDA 13) and theres a consistent ~20-30% throughput regression on SM90 for long-seq (2k) workloads. KV grow looks normal but per-token latency variance spikes.

alex: ugh. any obvious kernel selection diffs? Triton fallback? :thinking_face:

raj: Not obvious. profiler snapshot shows more time in memory wait / l2 stalls on SM90. Kernel chosen is the same fused-paged Flash variant, but launch params differ (sm90 picks larger block dims).

emily: can you paste the perf counters / nvprof-ish snippet? also which build (cuda/toolkit)

raj: build: runtime v2.9.1, cuda 13.1, triton 2.6. kernel_id: flash_paged_fused_v3. probe run commands: `./bench --model=16B --seq=2048 --batch=1 --variant=flash_paged_fused_v3 --prefetch=on`

raj: profiler snippet (top lines):
```
GPU time breakdown:
  kernel_flash_paged_fused_v3  12.4ms  (was 9.6ms on sm80)
  mem_copy_kv                 1.8ms   (same)
  prefetch_worker             0.9ms   (up 0.5ms)
Counters:
  l2_read_hit_rate  62% (was 78% on sm80)
  tensor_core_util  81% (small drop)
  avg_warp_occupancy  52% (was 68%)
  l2_pending_writes  increased x2
```

alex: l2 hit drop + occupancy drop = either changed tiling or prefetch alignment. could be a register-pressure change on sm90 causing more spills -> memory churn.

perf-runner-bot: Ran variant-compare matrix for raj at 2469123475: tried
  - flash_paged_fused_v2 (cuda kernels) -> SM90: 10.1ms
  - flash_paged_fused_v3 (triton)      -> SM90: 12.4ms
  - flash_paged_fused_v3 (cuda compiled) -> SM90: 11.8ms
  TL;DR: Triton v3 path is adding ~3-4% more overhead vs cuda jit, but majority of regression remains even with cuda compiled v3.

emily: interesting. so Triton adds small overhead, but main delta between sm80/sm90 remains. what about quantization / layout differences? maybe sm90's wider warp scheduling interacts with tiled prefetch pattern.

raj: I tried forcing smaller block dims (override cfg kernel.launch.block_x=256) on sm90 and it recovered ~10% of perf and improved occupancy to ~60%. L2 hit rate improved to 70%. But still ~10% behind sm80.

alex: can we try disabling prefetch to isolate? if prefetch causes misaligned L2 streaming on sm90, disabling should help or at least change profile.

raj: disabled prefetch -> kernel down to 10.5ms on sm90 (closer to sm80). But end-to-end token cost increases (more mem copy spikes). log: `prefetch=off improved occupancy but increased mem_copy_kv by 0.9ms`

emily: sounds like prefetch heuristic needs an SM-specific tuning knob. Maybe the runtime should pick prefetch=off for sequences >1k on SM90 unless block dims tuned. Could add heuristic: if l2_hit_rate<70% and occupancy<60% then try smaller blocks / disable prefetch.

alex: agree. also file a perf regression issue and include the microbench scripts + nvprof captures. @raj can you bisect commit range for kernel heuristics changes between our sm80 baseline build and the sm90 build?

raj: filing issue now (ENG-RT-#1249). attaching perf-runner outputs and config. Will run bisect tomorrow morning; adding quick mitigation: runtime flag `force_kernel_launch=sm80_compat` to force smaller blocks for sm90 sessions.

perf-runner-bot: Note: scheduled nightly matrix (sm80 vs sm90) to include `prefetch=on/off` permutations and Triton vs cuda kernel builds. Results will post in this thread. :white_check_mark:

emily: perfect. thanks — this one is subtle but actionable. once bisect narrows commits we can decide whether kernel selector or compiler heuristics need patching. :rocket:
